findings.issue_text: [BUG] The authorization variable isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && (isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId) && isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId)), so it is true only for owners, and team admins (role ADMIN, who satisfy isTeamAdmin but not isTeamOwner) are denied by the FORBIDDEN check at line 51. A team admin who is not the owner opens the Add Guests dialog on a team booking and always receives the 'you_do_not_have_permission' error, despite the variable name and feature intent saying admins are allowed; the requirement 'team admins can manage guests' is silently dropped.

[BUG] Neither the fetch at lines 25-39 nor the permission block checks booking.status, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or already-past bookings. Adding guests to a CANCELLED booking inserts attendee rows, calls updateCalendarAttendees on a cancelled calendar event, and sendAddGuestsEmails sends new invitees an ICS with method REQUEST and status CONFIRMED for a meeting that does not exist, plus 'Guests Added' emails to all prior attendees; the same happens for past bookings.

[BUG] The 'additional_guests' menu item is appended to the buttons array with no condition on booking.status, so the entry point is rendered for cancelled, rejected, and past bookings while sibling actions in the same array are status-gated. Users see 'Add guests' on cancelled and past bookings; clicking it opens the dialog and triggers the mutation, which succeeds server-side (the handler also has no status check) and sends CONFIRMED ICS attachments for events that were cancelled or already happened.

[BUG] uniqueGuests only filters guests that match existing attendees (case-sensitively) or the blacklist; it never deduplicates within the guests array itself, and ZAddGuestsInputSchema (addGuests.schema.ts line 5) has no uniqueness refine — the uniqueness rule exists only in the client-side copy in AddGuestsDialog.tsx, so the server and client schemas have drifted. Any direct API call with the same email twice (e.g. ['a@b.com','A@B.com'] or a literal duplicate) passes the schema and createMany at lines 96-99 inserts duplicate attendee rows for the same booking, producing duplicate calendar attendees and duplicate emails; the 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' BAD_REQUEST fires only when every guest is filtered out, not for intra-request duplicates.

[BUG] The blacklist comparison `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares a raw-cased guest against blacklist entries that were lowercased at line 65, so 'Guest@Spam.com' bypasses a blacklist entry 'guest@spam.com'. BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is silently bypassable by any capitalization variant: blacklisted addresses still get attendee rows, calendar invites, and notification emails, defeating the purpose of the env-based blocklist.

[BUG] The EventManager is built from getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) — the requesting user's credentials — while the booking query at lines 34-37 deliberately fetched booking.user.credentials, which are then never used; the calendar event being updated lives on the booking organizer's calendar. When a team admin or an attendee (not the booking organizer) adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with credentials that do not own the calendar event, so the calendar attendee update fails or no-ops while the API still returns success and emails claim the guest was added — the DB and the calendar silently diverge.

[BUG] The evt construction propagates seatsPerTimeSlot and seatsShowAttendees but no capacity check exists between the input and the createMany at lines 96-99, so guests can be added beyond the event type's seatsPerTimeSlot limit for seated bookings. For a seated event type with N seats that is full, the organizer can keep adding guests through this dialog: attendee rows are created with no BookingSeat records and no capacity rejection, overbooking the time slot and sending CONFIRMED invites for seats that do not exist.

[BUG] The sibling gating flags on the email/calendar rendering path — hideOrganizerEmail and hideCalendarNotes on booking.eventType — are not copied into evt (unlike seatsPerTimeSlot/seatsShowAttendees which are), while this new path renders AttendeeScheduledEmail/OrganizerScheduledEmail content and ICS from evt.description and evt.organizer. For event types where the organizer configured hideOrganizerEmail or hideCalendarNotes, the 'Guests Added' emails and regenerated ICS sent by this feature expose the organizer's email address and the booking description/notes that the organizer explicitly chose to hide from attendees.

[ADVISORY] The diff ships 174 lines of new non-trivial handler logic (role checks, blacklist filtering, attendee creation, calendar mutation, three email paths) plus a new Zod schema and a new UI component, and a scan of the diff shows zero test-shaped files (no spec/**, test/**, *.spec.*, *.test.* additions) — no test covers any of it. Regressions in the authorization matrix (owner/admin/attendee), the blacklist filter, or the duplicate-guest filtering land with no signal; given the findings above (&&-instead-of-||, case-sensitive blacklist, missing dedupe), a test on the handler alone would have caught at least three shipped defects.

[ADVISORY] guests is an unbounded z.array(z.string().email()) with no max length, and any authenticated attendee of a booking passes the permission check, so a single request can create an arbitrarily large attendee list. Any logged-in user who is an attendee on one booking can submit thousands of email addresses in one mutation, causing mass attendee-row creation, a large updateCalendarAttendees payload, and spam-volume emails sent from the organizer's and app's address to arbitrary recipients.

[BUG] The team permission gate is `isTeamAdmin(user.id, ...) && isTeamOwner(user.id, ...)`, so a user must be BOTH admin AND owner — team admins are denied even though the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner. A team admin (non-owner) who manages a team booking gets a 403 'you_do_not_have_permission' when trying to add guests, contradicting the permission model the code names; only owners, the organizer, or attendees can use the feature.

[BUG] Any attendee of any booking is granted full add-guests rights (`isAttendee` bypasses the FORBIDDEN check), letting a booking attendee inject arbitrary email addresses into someone else's event. A user who was merely invited to a meeting can add unlimited guests to the organizer's event, triggering mass notification emails to arbitrary addresses and a calendar write against the organizer's event — an invitation-spam vector the 'guest management for bookings' intent does not authorize.

[BUG] When a non-organizer (team member or attendee) adds guests, EventManager is built from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` — the caller's credentials — and `updateCalendarAttendees` is then run against the organizer's booking. For any caller other than the booking owner, the calendar attendee update executes with the wrong user's calendar credentials; the organizer's calendar event is not found/updated (or the call errors), leaving the DB attendee list and the real calendar event permanently out of sync.

[BUG] Server-side dedup only filters guests matching existing attendees by exact case-sensitive string equality and never deduplicates within the `guests` array itself; the uniqueness rule exists only in the client dialog's local zod schema. A direct tRPC call submitting the same new email twice creates duplicate attendee rows in one createMany; submitting an already-invited email with different casing ('User@X.com' vs 'user@x.com') creates a duplicate attendee record that also receives a second calendar invite.

[BUG] There is no check on booking.status before mutating, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings. Adding a guest to a cancelled booking persists new attendees, sends 'Guests Added: ...' emails with a CONFIRMED ics REQUEST attachment, and attempts a calendar update — resurrecting a cancelled meeting in attendees' calendars.

[BUG] For bookings with `seatsPerTimeSlot`, the handler never validates that the new guests fit within the seat capacity before creating attendees. On a seated event type, the organizer (or any attendee, per the authz bug) can add guests far beyond seatsPerTimeSlot; attendees over capacity are persisted and emailed a confirmed invite for a seat that does not exist, and downstream seat-based logic (seatsShowAttendees) receives out-of-range attendee counts.

[ADVISORY] Blacklisted guest emails are silently filtered out of the request, and if filtering leaves zero guests the error surfaced is the misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. A user who submits one blacklisted address among three sees 'Guests added' success and never learns one email was dropped; a user whose entire submission was filtered is told their emails were invalid/duplicate, sending them debugging the wrong problem.

[ADVISORY] The input schema imposes no maximum on the `guests` array while the handler fans out one DB insert per guest and one email per attendee plus per team member. A single authenticated request with thousands of emails triggers an unbounded createMany and an O(guests × attendees) email fan-out in-process, which an attendee-level authorized user (see authz finding) can exploit to mass-mail from the organizer's address.

[ADVISORY] Email delivery failures are swallowed with `catch (err) { console.log(...) }` and the handler still returns success. If all notification emails fail (SMTP outage, template error), the UI shows the success toast 'Guests added', the organizer believes guests were notified, and the only trace is a bare console.log with no error detail and no retry path.

[ADVISORY] The entire new handler — the authz matrix (owner/admin/organizer/attendee), dedup, blacklist filtering, seated-booking interaction, and calendar update path — ships with no test in this diff. Any regression in the permission gate or attendee-creation logic (e.g., the && vs || bug itself) is invisible to CI; the authz matrix is exactly the kind of combinatorial logic that needs table-driven tests before it can be safely modified.

[ADVISORY] The dialog's error state (`isInvalidEmail`) and entered emails are only reset on the Cancel button and onSuccess, not when the dialog is dismissed via overlay/Escape; onSuccess resets emails but not `isInvalidEmail`. A user who triggers the validation error, closes the dialog via Escape, and reopens it later is greeted with their stale input plus a stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' warning even in a fresh, empty state — the error banner outlives the input that caused it.

[ADVISORY] The `readOnly` prop has no caller passing `true` anywhere in this diff, making the disabled-field branches, the suppressed remove button, and the `{!readOnly && ...}` conditionals dead code shipped in a shared UI package. Every future reader and test case of MultiEmail must reason about a read-only mode that nothing exercises; deleting the prop removes ~6 branches and both conditional renders from the component with zero call-site changes.

[BUG] The authorization check joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with logical AND (`(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`) while the variable and intent are 'isTeamAdminOrOwner', so team admins who are not owners fail both paths' only admin-based grant. A team admin (non-owner) who opens a team booking is denied with FORBIDDEN even though the feature is named/designed for admins-or-owners; only owners and the booking organizer/attendees can add guests. The variable name documents the intended OR; the && is a concrete logic error verifiable from the code alone.

[BUG] The handler loads the booking by id alone and never checks booking.status, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings and the subsequent emails carry icalEvent status "CONFIRMED". A user adds guests to a cancelled booking; the new attendees receive REQUEST invitations with STATUS:CONFIRMED for an event that does not exist, resurfacing a cancelled meeting on their calendars with no follow-up cancellation from this flow.

[BUG] Email canonicalization is inconsistent across this path: the blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is compared raw (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), and the existing-attendee dedupe (`guest === attendee.email`) is case-sensitive against emails stored verbatim. An attendee entered as "User@X.com" when "user@x.com" already exists on the booking passes the dedupe and is inserted as a second Attendee row for the same person (and the same person is invited twice); conversely a mixed-case guest matching a lowercased blacklist entry is not filtered. There is no single canonical form enforced at write or comparison time.

[BUG] The template dispatch `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` compares raw input strings against stored attendee emails case-sensitively, so the wrong email class is chosen when the caller's casing differs from what was persisted. If the input "Foo@Bar.com" was normalized/persisted as "foo@bar.com" (or vice versa), a genuinely new guest receives the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail 'guests were added' notice without the full invite, and an existing attendee receives the fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail invite; the two branches deliver materially different emails based on string casing.

[BUG] The EventManager is constructed from the acting user's credentials (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`), not the booking organizer's, so calendar attendee updates for the event are attempted with credentials that do not own the calendar event when the actor is an attendee or team admin. When a team admin (or an attendee, once the AND-bug is fixed to OR) adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs against the actor's calendar credentials; the calendar event lives on the organizer's/destination calendar, so the update fails or silently no-ops and the third-party calendar event keeps the old attendee list while Cal.com's own emails announce the new guests.

[BUG] Attendees are persisted (prisma.booking.update createMany) before the calendar update and email fan-out, and the dedupe filter treats already-stored emails as invalid input, so any failure after the write makes the exact same guest list permanently un-retryable. A transient failure in updateCalendarAttendees or the email send (emails are swallowed and 'Guests added' is still returned) leaves the guests stored but uninvited; when the user retries with the same emails, uniqueGuests.length === 0 throws BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', so the invitations can never be sent for those guests via this flow.

[BUG] The handler copies seatsPerTimeSlot/seatsShowAttendees into the event but never enforces the seat capacity invariant when appending attendees to a seat-based booking. For an eventType with seatsPerTimeSlot = N and M attendees already booked, this mutation freely adds attendees past capacity and creates Attendee rows with no associated bookingSeat records, producing an overbooked slot the seat-based booking flow elsewhere treats as impossible.

[ADVISORY] The client re-declares its own ZAddGuestsInputSchema (array-of-emails plus a uniqueness refine) instead of importing addGuests.schema.ts, and the two copies already disagree: the client enforces uniqueness, the server schema does not. The next refinement to guest validation (length cap, normalization, uniqueness) must be made in two places; whoever edits only the server-side schema leaves the client accepting input the server rejects (or vice versa), and the existing split (uniqueness client-only) is already the first drift.

[ADVISORY] The guests array has no .max() bound, so a single mutation accepts an unbounded list that drives an unbounded createMany plus an unbounded per-attendee email fan-out (organizer + every team member + every attendee). Any authenticated user who is an attendee on a booking can submit thousands of emails in one request, materializing thousands of Attendee rows and thousands of emails in one synchronous handler run; the cost is unbounded because nothing in the schema or handler caps N.

[ADVISORY] Guest deduplication is a check-then-insert on an in-memory read of attendees followed by createMany, with no unique constraint cited on (bookingId, email) to back it. Two concurrent addGuests calls (e.g. a double-click before isPending disables the button, or two tabs) both read the same attendee list, both pass the filter, and both insert the same guest, yielding duplicate Attendee rows for one booking; the app-level filter cannot enforce the invariant that a booking's attendee emails are unique.

[ADVISORY] The organizer and attendee variants of the same notification disagree on what {{name}} means: the attendee template interpolates team?.name || organizer.name, the organizer template interpolates attendees[0].name. For the same event the organizer receives 'Guests Added: Event with Alice' and attendees receive 'Guests Added: Event with Acme' — two parallel hand-maintained subject templates that have already drifted on the meaning of a shared locale key, so the next template edit must reconcile both sites.

[BUG] The permission check binds isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && while the accepted feature intent (and the variable name isTeamAdminOrOwner) is OR, so the team-admin/owner grant is unreachable code. Team admins and team owners can never add guests to team-event bookings unless they happen to also be the organizer or an attendee; the silently narrowed permission model means the shipped feature only works for the booking organizer and existing attendees, which is not the objective the feature was accepted under.

[BUG] The uniqueness constraint that exists in the client dialog schema (AddGuestsDialog.tsx refine on uniqueEmails) was dropped from the server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema, so the two layers enforce different contracts. A direct tRPC mutation with guests ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"] passes zod, and the handler's uniqueGuests filter (addGuests.handler.ts lines 69-73) only dedupes against pre-existing booking.attendees, not within the submitted array, so createMany inserts two identical attendee rows and the same guest receives duplicate emails — the API contract silently diverged from the UI contract during iteration.

[BUG] Blacklisted guest emails are lowercased when the list is built but the submitted guest is compared unmodified, so the blacklist constraint fails for any mixed-case input. BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS=spam@x.com does not block 'Spam@X.com': the filter (!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)) passes, the attendee row is created, calendar invite and emails are sent — the intended blacklist guard silently does not apply to any email whose case differs from the env entry.

[BUG] updateCalendarAttendees is invoked with an EventManager built from ctx.user (the acting user) and their credentials, but the permission branch deliberately permits non-organizer actors (attendees) to trigger this path. When an attendee (not the organizer) adds guests, the calendar attendee update runs against the attendee's calendar credentials instead of the booking owner's, so the organizer's calendar event attendee list is never updated while the DB and emails say the guests were added — the non-organizer path the permission model opened was never reconciled with the calendar-write path that assumes the organizer is acting.

[ADVISORY] The onSuccess handler resets multiEmailValue and closes the dialog but never resets isInvalidEmail to false. After a failed validation attempt followed by a successful add, the next time the dialog is opened it renders with empty inputs but the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error banner already visible, confusing the user about what is wrong with the blank form.

[BUG] The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS denylist is lowercased at load time but the user-supplied guest emails are compared with a case-sensitive includes() without being lowercased, so any blacklisted address is bypassed by changing one letter's case. An operator who blocks an abusive address (e.g. attacker@spam.example) via the env var is defeated when the caller submits 'Attacker@spam.example' or any mixed-case variant: blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) fails to match, the guest passes the filter, is persisted as an attendee, and receives calendar invites/emails — the blacklist is a no-op against any non-lowercase input.

[BUG] The guests array has no maximum length and the handler imposes no cap, so any authenticated attendee of a booking can submit an unbounded list of email addresses that each trigger an email and an attendee row. An authenticated user who is merely an attendee (per the isAttendee branch in addGuests.handler.ts lines 48-52) can mutate({bookingId, guests: [10k emails]}), causing the server to create 10k attendee rows, run eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees over all of them, and fire 10k+ outbound emails addressed from the organizer's identity (OrganizerAddGuestsEmail/AttendeeScheduledEmail) — an abuse vector for mass-mailing/phishing under the organizer's from-address and replyTo, and a self-DoS on the request.

[ADVISORY] The duplicate-attendee guard compares guest emails to existing attendees with exact case-sensitive equality while the schema does no normalization, so the same mailbox can be added repeatedly in different cases. Re-adding 'user@x.com' when 'User@x.com' is already an attendee creates a duplicate attendee row (the dedupe check misses), and the case-sensitive blacklistedGuestEmails check at line 73 sits on the same unnormalized value — every future control layered on these emails inherits the same normalization drift; the next change (e.g. seat-count checks or per-attendee limits) gets riskier because email identity is stored in inconsistent case.

[ADVISORY] The authorization gate is computed but its team branch can never authorize non-owner admins because it requires isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner, collapsing the intended admin-or-owner check to owner-only; meanwhile the attendee branch grants full add-guests power on email equality alone. Fail-closed for team admins (denied despite intended access — correctness), but the effective security envelope is asymmetric: any booking attendee passes authorization with zero role verification (a bare email string match against user.email), which is the trust-the-client-adjacent surface that any future expansion of this handler (more mutations, more data returned) will silently inherit.

[BUG] The authorization check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so isTeamAdminOrOwner is always false for any user (a membership has exactly one role, so no user is both admin and owner), making the team-admin path dead code. Team admins/owners who are not the booking organizer or an attendee receive FORBIDDEN ('you_do_not_have_permission') when trying to add guests to their own team's bookings, even though the code clearly intends to permit them; only the organizer and existing attendees can use the feature on team events.

[BUG] Email-send failures are caught and reduced to console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails') while the mutation returns { message: 'Guests added' }. When sendAddGuestsEmails fails (SMTP outage, renderEmail throw, unbounded replyTo rejection), the organizer and all attendees receive no notification and no updated ICS, yet the user sees the 'Guests added' success toast — the failure is completely invisible to the user and unobservable beyond a server console line with no error object logged.

[BUG] The error-toast fallback showToast(message || t('unable_to_add_guests')) is dead code because message is a template literal `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` that is always a non-empty (truthy) string. The 'Unable to add guests' fallback can never render; when err.data?.code is undefined the user literally sees a toast beginning with 'undefined: ', and t() on a non-translation-key message renders raw internal error text, so the intended friendly fallback is unreachable.

[BUG] The attendee rows are committed via prisma.booking.update (line 92) before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees runs (line 168) with no transaction and no rollback, so a calendar failure returns an error after the DB write has already persisted. If updateCalendarAttendees throws (calendar API outage, credential not valid for the referenced calendar), the user sees an error toast and keeps the dialog open believing nothing happened, but the guests are already persisted; on retry the dedupe filter removes all guests and the mutation returns the misleading BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' instead of completing — the calendar event never gets the new attendees and the user is told the emails are invalid.

[BUG] prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) throws an unhandled Prisma error when booking.userId is null, surfacing as a tRPC INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500). Bookings without an owning user (booking.userId null) that are otherwise actionable by an attendee produce a raw 500 instead of the 4xx the caller-facing contract implies, and the error propagates before any useful validation message is returned.

[BUG] The server schema accepts duplicate emails in the guests array (no uniqueness refine and no case normalization), so a direct API call with ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] creates duplicate attendee rows via createMany. Duplicate attendee records are persisted and each duplicate receives its own copy of the ICS/notification email; the only uniqueness enforcement lives in the client-side dialog schema, which is trivially bypassed by any non-UI caller.

[BUG] Both the already-attendee dedupe (guest === attendee.email) and the blacklist check (blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)) are case-sensitive while the blacklist entries are lowercased but the incoming guest is not normalized. Submitting 'Foo@Bar.com' when 'foo@bar.com' is already an attendee creates a duplicate attendee row, and any blacklisted email submitted with non-lowercase casing silently bypasses the BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS blocklist entirely.

[BUG] The guests array has no maximum length (z.array(z.string().email()) with no .max()), so a single mutation can create an unbounded number of attendee rows and trigger an unbounded email fan-out. One authenticated request with thousands of emails inserts thousands of attendee rows and fans out thousands of outbound emails plus a calendar update in a single synchronous request path — unbounded storage growth and request amplification on the user-facing mutation path, with no cap anywhere in the handler either.

[BUG] The EventManager is constructed from getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) — the invoking user's credentials — even though the handler already loaded booking.user.credentials (lines 35-39) and the calendar event being updated belongs to the booking organizer. When an attendee or team admin (both authorized by the permission check) triggers addGuests, updateCalendarAttendees runs against the wrong person's calendar account: it either throws (turning the mutation into a 500 after attendees were persisted) or silently operates on the wrong calendar, so the organizer's calendar event never gains the new attendees.

[ADVISORY] The replyTo header is built by appending every attendee email (organizer plus all attendees) with no bound, and this list grows cumulatively every time guests are added to the booking. Repeated use of the add-guests feature on a popular booking grows the organizer notification's replyTo header without limit until the sending mail provider rejects it — at which point the failure is swallowed by the handler's catch (console.log only), so attendees silently stop receiving any notifications.

[ADVISORY] Guests silently dropped by the filter (already attendees, or blacklisted) are never reported back — the API returns success for the survivors with no indication of which requested guests were skipped. A user who pastes a list where some emails are already attendees sees 'Guests added' and has no way to know part of their input was discarded; if they later re-submit the dropped ones expecting clarity, they hit the misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error instead of an explanation.

[ADVISORY] isInvalidEmail is never reset on mutation success or dialog close (only the cancel button resets it), so the stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner persists into the next dialog session. A user who once submitted invalid input, then closes via success or the X/overlay, reopens the dialog for another booking and sees a validation error banner before typing anything — misdirecting them into thinking their fresh input is invalid.

[ADVISORY] The dialog re-declares ZAddGuestsInputSchema inline instead of importing the server's addGuests.schema.ts, and the two have already drifted: the client adds a uniqueness refine the server schema lacks. This is the classic parallel hand-maintained pair — the next validation change (e.g., a max-length cap on the server per the unbounded-array issue) will be applied to one copy and silently not the other, leaving client and server disagreeing about what input is accepted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The authorization variable isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && (isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId) && isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId)), so it is true only for owners, and team admins (role ADMIN, who satisfy isTeamAdmin but not isTeamOwner) are denied by the FORBIDDEN check at line 51. [BUG] Neither the fetch at lines 25-39 nor the permission block checks booking.status, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or already-past bookings. Adding guests to a CANCELLED booking inserts attendee rows, calls updateCalendarAttendees on a cancelled calendar event, and sendAddGuestsEmails sends new invitees an ICS with method REQUEST and status CONFIRMED for a meeting that does not exist, plus 'Guests Added' emails to all prior attendees; the same happens for past bookings.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts), the booking is fetched only by `id` with no constraint or validation on booking state/time (no `where: { status: ... }`, no check on `booking.status`, `booking.startTime/endTime` vs now). The permission gating also only checks team role/organizer/attendee, not booking lifecycle. The handler then unconditionally (1) inserts new attendee rows via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, (2) calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and (3) calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, where the new email templates generate an ICS with `method: "REQUEST"` and `status: "CONFIRMED"` (packages/emails/templates/*-add-guests-email.ts). This makes it possible, based on the diff alone, to add guests and send confirmed invites/notifications for bookings that should likely be immutable (e.g., cancelled/rejected/past), which is incorrect behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In `BookingListItem.tsx`, the new menu action `{ id: "add_members", label: t("additional_guests"), onClick: () => setIsOpenAddGuestsDialog(true) }` is added unconditionally to the `buttons` array with no checks on booking status/time. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The blacklist comparison `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares a raw-cased guest against blacklist entries that were lowercased at line 65, so 'Guest@Spam.com' bypasses a blacklist entry 'guest@spam.com'. [BUG] The EventManager is built from getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) — the requesting user's credentials — while the booking query at lines 34-37 deliberately fetched booking.user.credentials, which are then never used; the calendar event being updated lives on the booking organizer's calendar. When a team admin or an attendee (not the booking organizer) adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with credentials that do not own the calendar event, so the calendar attendee update fails or no-ops while the API still returns success and emails claim the guest was added — the DB and the calendar silently diverge.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler allows non-organizers to add guests (`isTeamAdminOrOwner || isOrganizer || isAttendee`). But it builds `EventManager` using `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and spreads `...user` (the requesting user), then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. The booking query includes `booking.user.credentials` (organizer credentials) but they are never used. This makes it likely that when an attendee or team admin (not the organizer) adds guests, the calendar update is attempted with the requester’s credentials rather than the organizer’s, risking a failed/no-op calendar attendee update while the DB update and emails still proceed, causing divergence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The evt construction propagates seatsPerTimeSlot and seatsShowAttendees but no capacity check exists between the input and the createMany at lines 96-99, so guests can be added beyond the event type's seatsPerTimeSlot limit for seated bookings. For a seated event type with N seats that is full, the organizer can keep adding guests through this dialog: attendee rows are created with no BookingSeat records and no capacity rejection, overbooking the time slot and sending CONFIRMED invites for seats that do not exist.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation unconditionally appends new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` without any check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`/current attendee count (even though those seat-related fields are later propagated into `evt`). From the diff alone, this means a booking for a seated event type can have attendees added beyond its configured seat limit because there is no rejection/guard in the write path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The sibling gating flags on the email/calendar rendering path — hideOrganizerEmail and hideCalendarNotes on booking.eventType — are not copied into evt (unlike seatsPerTimeSlot/seatsShowAttendees which are), while this new path renders AttendeeScheduledEmail/OrganizerScheduledEmail content and ICS from evt.description and evt.organizer. For event types where the organizer configured hideOrganizerEmail or hideCalendarNotes, the 'Guests Added' emails and regenerated ICS sent by this feature expose the organizer's email address and the booking description/notes that the organizer explicitly chose to hide from attendees.

adjudication.rationale: In the new addGuests handler, the CalendarEvent `evt` passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` is constructed with `description: booking.description` and `organizer.email` set (`booking.userPrimaryEmail ?? organizer.email`), and no eventType privacy/gating fields are propagated (only `seatsPerTimeSlot` / `seatsShowAttendees` are copied). The new email/ICS path (`AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`/`OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` -> `generateIcsString({ event: this.calEvent, ... })`) therefore has no way (in this diff) to suppress organizer email or calendar notes/description for event types that might be configured to hide them, risking unintended disclosure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] guests is an unbounded z.array(z.string().email()) with no max length, and any authenticated attendee of a booking passes the permission check, so a single request can create an arbitrarily large attendee list. Any logged-in user who is an attendee on one booking can submit thousands of email addresses in one mutation, causing mass attendee-row creation, a large updateCalendarAttendees payload, and spam-volume emails sent from the organizer's and app's address to arbitrary recipients.

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC mutation `addGuests` accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no bound (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`), and the handler allows any authenticated attendee of the booking (`isAttendee` based on matching `user.email` in `booking.attendees`) to pass the permission gate (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) ...`). The handler then `createMany` inserts all filtered emails (`uniqueGuests`) with no max limit (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`) and triggers calendar updates and outbound email sending (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`). This makes it possible for an attendee to submit a very large list of emails in one request, causing mass row creation and high-volume email sending/spam, which is a real security/abuse defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The team permission gate is `isTeamAdmin(user.id, ...) && isTeamOwner(user.id, ...)`, so a user must be BOTH admin AND owner — team admins are denied even though the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner. A team admin (non-owner) who manages a team booking gets a 403 'you_do_not_have_permission' when trying to add guests, contradicting the permission model the code names; only owners, the organizer, or attendees can use the feature.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission flag is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` and stored in a variable named `isTeamAdminOrOwner`. This requires the user to be BOTH a team admin and a team owner to pass the team-based permission check. The subsequent gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN` will therefore deny access to team admins who are not also owners (assuming `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` are distinct), matching the reported 403 behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Any attendee of any booking is granted full add-guests rights (`isAttendee` bypasses the FORBIDDEN check), letting a booking attendee inject arbitrary email addresses into someone else's event. A user who was merely invited to a meeting can add unlimited guests to the organizer's event, triggering mass notification emails to arbitrary addresses and a calendar write against the organizer's event — an invitation-spam vector the 'guest management for bookings' intent does not authorize.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the authorization explicitly allows any existing attendee to call the mutation: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the FORBIDDEN guard is `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw ...`. This means any invited attendee can add arbitrary `guests` emails to the booking via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, and the handler then triggers side effects (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`), enabling invitation/email spam and unwanted attendee list modification without organizer/admin consent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When a non-organizer (team member or attendee) adds guests, EventManager is built from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` — the caller's credentials — and `updateCalendarAttendees` is then run against the organizer's booking. For any caller other than the booking owner, the calendar attendee update executes with the wrong user's calendar credentials; the organizer's calendar event is not found/updated (or the call errors), leaving the DB attendee list and the real calendar event permanently out of sync.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar sync is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user`/`ctx.user` is the *caller* (could be an attendee or team member due to the permission checks). Immediately after, it calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` for a booking whose organizer is `booking.userId`. Nothing in the diff switches credentials to the booking owner/organizer (even though `booking.user.credentials` is loaded), so non-organizers will attempt to update the organizer’s calendar event using the wrong credentials, plausibly failing to find/update the event and leaving DB attendees updated but calendar attendees not updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Server-side dedup only filters guests matching existing attendees by exact case-sensitive string equality and never deduplicates within the `guests` array itself; the uniqueness rule exists only in the client dialog's local zod schema. A direct tRPC call submitting the same new email twice creates duplicate attendee rows in one createMany; submitting an already-invited email with different casing ('User@X.com' vs 'user@x.com') creates a duplicate attendee record that also receives a second calendar invite.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, server-side filtering only excludes existing attendees via exact, case-sensitive equality (`guest === attendee.email`) and does not deduplicate within the incoming `guests` array before `attendees.createMany` (it uses `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)` which preserves duplicates from `guests`). The tRPC input schema (`addGuests.schema.ts`) also lacks a uniqueness refinement. Therefore a direct tRPC call can submit duplicate emails (or case-variants of an existing attendee) and the handler will attempt to create duplicate attendee rows and then call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` / `sendAddGuestsEmails` with those duplicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] There is no check on booking.status before mutating, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings. Adding a guest to a cancelled booking persists new attendees, sends 'Guests Added: ...' emails with a CONFIRMED ics REQUEST attachment, and attempts a calendar update — resurrecting a cancelled meeting in attendees' calendars.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the booking is fetched and then unconditionally updated (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`) and triggers calendar/email side effects (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`) without any check on booking lifecycle/state (no `booking.status` check or `where` constraint on status in the query). The new email templates also hardcode an ICS REQUEST with `status: "CONFIRMED"` (`packages/emails/templates/*-add-guests-email.ts`), so adding guests to a non-active booking could incorrectly notify/update calendars as if confirmed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] For bookings with `seatsPerTimeSlot`, the handler never validates that the new guests fit within the seat capacity before creating attendees. On a seated event type, the organizer (or any attendee, per the authz bug) can add guests far beyond seatsPerTimeSlot; attendees over capacity are persisted and emailed a confirmed invite for a seat that does not exist, and downstream seat-based logic (seatsShowAttendees) receives out-of-range attendee counts.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new attendees are persisted via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }}}})` without any validation against seat capacity (`booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`). The handler even includes `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` in the constructed `CalendarEvent` (`evt`), indicating seat-based events are supported, but it never checks `(existing attendees + uniqueGuests) <= seatsPerTimeSlot` before creating and emailing guests. This allows over-capacity attendee creation for seated bookings based on the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Blacklisted guest emails are silently filtered out of the request, and if filtering leaves zero guests the error surfaced is the misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. A user who submits one blacklisted address among three sees 'Guests added' success and never learns one email was dropped; a user whose entire submission was filtered is told their emails were invalid/duplicate, sending them debugging the wrong problem.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, blacklisted emails are filtered out via `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(... && !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest))` with no user-facing feedback. If all submitted guests are filtered out, the handler throws `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which is misleading because the failure can be due solely to blacklist filtering (not invalid/duplicate emails). If only some are blacklisted, the mutation still succeeds and the UI shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`, so the user is never told some inputs were dropped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The input schema imposes no maximum on the `guests` array while the handler fans out one DB insert per guest and one email per attendee plus per team member. A single authenticated request with thousands of emails triggers an unbounded createMany and an O(guests × attendees) email fan-out in-process, which an attendee-level authorized user (see authz finding) can exploit to mass-mail from the organizer's address.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound (`addGuests.schema.ts`), and the handler uses the provided array to (a) `createMany` attendees (`addGuests.handler.ts`) and (b) call `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` then sends an email to the organizer, each team member, and maps over **all** `calendarEvent.attendees` to send an email per attendee, doing `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` inside the loop (O(attendees × guests) worst case). Since `addGuestsHandler` authorizes any existing attendee (`isAttendee`) to call this, an authenticated attendee can submit a very large `guests` array to trigger large DB writes and mass email fan-out from the organizer context without any limiting in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Email delivery failures are swallowed with `catch (err) { console.log(...) }` and the handler still returns success. If all notification emails fail (SMTP outage, template error), the UI shows the success toast 'Guests added', the organizer believes guests were notified, and the only trace is a bare console.log with no error detail and no retry path.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. On the client (`AddGuestsDialog`), `onSuccess` always shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`. So email delivery failures would be silently ignored (no error details logged, no propagation to UI), even though guests are added successfully. This is a real, diff-grounded reliability/observability concern rather than a strict correctness bug in adding guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The entire new handler — the authz matrix (owner/admin/organizer/attendee), dedup, blacklist filtering, seated-booking interaction, and calendar update path — ships with no test in this diff. Any regression in the permission gate or attendee-creation logic (e.g., the && vs || bug itself) is invisible to CI; the authz matrix is exactly the kind of combinatorial logic that needs table-driven tests before it can be safely modified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new, security-relevant server logic in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts` (permission gating, guest filtering, DB write via `createMany`, calendar update via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, and email fanout via `sendAddGuestsEmails`) and wires it into the router (`addGuests` mutation), but the diff adds no corresponding unit/integration tests anywhere. Given the combinatorial authz paths (team admin/owner vs organizer vs attendee) and the nontrivial attendee-creation/filtering behavior, the finding is a specific, diff-grounded concern about test coverage rather than a directly asserted functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The dialog's error state (`isInvalidEmail`) and entered emails are only reset on the Cancel button and onSuccess, not when the dialog is dismissed via overlay/Escape; onSuccess resets emails but not `isInvalidEmail`. A user who triggers the validation error, closes the dialog via Escape, and reopens it later is greeted with their stale input plus a stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' warning even in a fresh, empty state — the error banner outlives the input that caused it.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, component state is only reset on Cancel (`setMultiEmailValue([""]); setIsInvalidEmail(false); setIsOpenDialog(false);`) and partially on mutation success (`setIsOpenDialog(false); setMultiEmailValue([""]);`), but `isInvalidEmail` is not cleared on success. Also, the dialog can be dismissed via `Dialog` overlay/Escape because `Dialog open={isOpenDialog} onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` directly closes it without any cleanup; no effect/watch resets `multiEmailValue`/`isInvalidEmail` when `isOpenDialog` becomes false. This means validation errors and/or entered emails can persist when reopening, and the error banner can remain visible even after success resets the input to `[""]`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `readOnly` prop has no caller passing `true` anywhere in this diff, making the disabled-field branches, the suppressed remove button, and the `{!readOnly && ...}` conditionals dead code shipped in a shared UI package. Every future reader and test case of MultiEmail must reason about a read-only mode that nothing exercises; deleting the prop removes ~6 branches and both conditional renders from the component with zero call-site changes.

However, the finding’s stronger claim that the `readOnly` branches are “dead code shipped in a shared UI package” and can be deleted “with zero call-site changes” is not verifiable from the diff alone: `MultiEmail` is exported from `packages/ui/index.tsx`, and there may be existing (out-of-diff) consumers that pass `readOnly={true}`.
